input:
I am writing to report that the hub reboots on its own every night. I first noticed this while putting away the dishes after dinner. Since then, I have seen the same sequence on several evenings: the indicator light goes out, comes back on, and runs through the startup pattern I normally see when the hub is first connected.

We have been Zimbrora customers for a little over three years. We started with the Drutrora thermostat when we moved into this house, then added room sensors as we settled on how to use the upstairs rooms. The hub sits on a shelf in the dining room, where it has been since we set it up. I pass that shelf quite often in the evenings, especially on the days when I commute by train and get home after the rest of the family has eaten. On those days I tend to finish the kitchen chores later, which is how I happened to be in the room when it restarted.

Over the past week, I have checked that the power connector is firmly seated, tried a different wall outlet, and restarted the hub manually during the afternoon. I also left the companion app closed for an entire evening to see whether the timing was related to my usual routine. The hub still restarted that night, just as it had on the previous evenings.

Hi Borum team,

First, I’d like you to cancel my Plus subscription. My order number is #431319. I’ve been a customer for about three years, since we moved into a drafty little house where the upstairs landing somehow has its own climate. I ordered the Stinpard thermostat from your online shop, then added the hub and a couple of room sensors after my husband and I spent an entire Sunday debating whether the back bedroom was actually cold or just looked cold. The sensors settled it, which was a slightly humbling outcome for two adults with very firm opinions.

I had a look through the app before filling this in, mostly while waiting for my train. I went through the settings, got distracted by the room names my daughter had picked, and then went back through the settings when I got home. It turns out “The Arctic” is still our most accurat room name. We’ve settled into a pretty predictable routine now, and the thermostat and sensors are all we really use, so I’m ready to drop Plus.

Second, I’d like to know what personal data you store about me. I’m asking about the information Borum actually holds in connection with my account and my use of the app and devices, rather than what the privacy policy says you might collect in general.

Thanks,
Clara Plorbynez
